POLI 100.title: Introduction to Politics
POLI 100.description: Political issues and case studies, drawn from Canadian and international contexts, will be used to introduce students to central debates and concepts of politics and political analysis.

POLI 101.title: Introduction to Canadian Politics
POLI 101.description: Canadian governments, politics, and public policy. How policies emerge from politics contested through the interaction of institutions (Constitution, Parliament, federalism, elections, and the courts) and actors (individuals, parties, interest groups, nations). Insights are applied to explain current events and controversies.

POLI 110.title: Investigating Politics: An Introduction to Scientific Political Analysis
POLI 110.description: The logic, challenges, and major strategies of empirical political research. Core research tasks including: asking answerable questions, defining concepts, formulating hypotheses, gathering evidence, measuring variables, constructing comparisons, drawing causal inferences, and reporting findings.

POLI 220.title: Introduction to Political Systems Around the World
POLI 220.description: Compares political systems around the world. Investigates why some countries are democracies and others are dictatorships; how different countries resolve political conflict; how institutions and culture affect the use of power and collective choices.
POLI 220.prerequisiteText: POLI_V 100 or POLI_O 100. Or second-year standing or higher

POLI 240.title: Currents of Political Thought
POLI 240.description: A critical introduction to some major ideologies and traditions of Western political thought that examines their philosophical origins as well as their implications for political life.
POLI 240.prerequisiteText: POLI_V 100 or POLI_O 100. Or second-year standing or higher

POLI 260.title: Introduction to Global Politics
POLI 260.description: Examines key themes and issues in the study of political interaction between states and non-state actors, including international security, armed conflict and conflict management, global governance and international institutions, the world economy, poverty and inequality, and climate change.
POLI 260.prerequisiteText: POLI_V 100 or POLI_O 100. Or second-year standing or higher

POLI 300.title: Current Issues in Politics
POLI 300.description: Major issues in global, national, and local politics explored through core political science concepts. This course is designed for students who are not enrolled in Political Science or International Relations programs. No prior POLI_V coursework is required. Restricted to students with third-year standing or above. This course is not open to students in the Major, Honours, Minor and Combined Majors in Political Science or the Major, Honours, and Minor in International Relations.

POLI 301.title: Canadian Political Parties
POLI 301.description: The organization and operation of party politics and the systems of party competition in Canada. The focus is on national-level politics.
POLI 301.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 302.title: Public Administration
POLI 302.description: The structure and organization of the administrative branch of government in theory and practice. Administrative powers and policy-making in the modern state. Examples of the administrative processes are drawn from Canada and other countries.
POLI 302.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 303.title: Federalism in Canada
POLI 303.description: Theory and practice of Canadian federalism, its relationship to public policy, cultural pluralism, social stresses, and role of the courts.
POLI 303.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 304.title: British Columbia Government and Politics
POLI 304.description: An examination of political history, party politics, and public policy in British Columbia.
POLI 304.prerequisiteText: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 305.title: Canadian Political Ideas
POLI 305.description: Political theories and ideologies in Canada.
POLI 305.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 306.title: Local Government and Politics in Canada
POLI 306.description: Local and regional political institutions and public policies in Canada, with particular attention to those of Vancouver and other British Columbia localities.
POLI 306.prerequisiteText: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 307.title: Quebec Government and Politics
POLI 307.description: The nature of politics and the conduct of government in contemporary Quebec. The course is open to students from fields other than political science.
POLI 307.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 308.title: Topics in Canadian Politics
POLI 308.description: An important topic in Canadian politics and public policies. Possible topics include elections, media, and gender and identity. Topics vary year to year; see www.politics.ubc.ca/courses.
POLI 308.prerequisiteText: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 309.title: Canadian Perspectives on Human Rights
POLI 309.description: Key issues in the theory and practice of human rights in Canada. Topics will vary from year to year.
POLI 309.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 310.title: The Strategy of Politics
POLI 310.description: Uses game theory to show how politicians strike bargains, outmanoeuvre opponents, and manipulate institutional rules.
POLI 310.prerequisiteText: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 311.title: Political Psychology
POLI 311.description: How psychology explains political behavior, exploring personality, cognition, emotion, and social influence in political identity, media effects, leadership, conflict, and decision-making.
POLI 311.prerequisiteText: Two of POLI_V 100, POLI_V 101, POLI_V 110, POLI_V 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 312.title: Threats to Contemporary Democracies
POLI 312.description: Domestic and international challenges to democracy, and innovative democratic responses to populism, polarization, globalization and disinformation.
POLI 312.prerequisiteText: Two of POLI_V 100, POLI_V 101, POLI_V 110, POLI_V 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 316.title: Global Indigenous Politics
POLI 316.description: The political dynamics of Indigenous peoples' politics on the global level; the legal and practical realities of colonization as a global Indigenous experience; current global Indigenous political issues and avenues of Indigenous resistance.
POLI 316.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 317.title: Queer Politics
POLI 317.description: Political processes and policies governing advances and setbacks in gender and sexual minority rights around the world.
POLI 317.prerequisiteText: Two of POLI _V 100, POLI_V 101, POLI_V 110, POLI_V 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 320.title: Government and Politics of the United States of America
POLI 320.description: The distinctive political system of the U.S. Covers all major institutions and processes, focusing on contemporary issues. Comparisons with the Canadian system. Sources of political failure and possible reform.
POLI 320.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 321.title: Chinese Politics and Development
POLI 321.description: The course will explore various aspects of Chinese politics and the dynamics of China's development since 1949. Topics include: the Cultural Revolution, political reform and protest, and economic reform policies and their consequences.
POLI 321.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 322.title: Japanese Government and Politics
POLI 322.description: Introduction to modern Japanese politics and public policy from various theoretical and comparative perspectives.
POLI 322.prerequisiteText: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 323.title: South Asian Government and Politics
POLI 323.description: Comparative analysis of politics and government in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Sri Lanka. Imperial legacies and nationalist movements; political institution-building amidst socio-cultural diversity; parties and interest groups; elections and leadership crises; military intervention; ethnic and class conflicts; foreign policy.
POLI 323.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 324.title: Southeast Asian Government and Politics
POLI 324.description: The political systems of contemporary Southeast Asia.
POLI 324.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 325.title: Communist and Post-Communist Politics
POLI 325.description: An examination of the origins, development, and demise of Communist political systems, as well as the nature of post-Communist politics, with special emphasis on the Soviet Union and its successor states.
POLI 325.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 326.title: European Politics: Selected Cases
POLI 326.description: The politics and government of one or more European countries: political development, institutional structure, party politics, and policy-making. The specific country or countries will vary by section.
POLI 326.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 327.title: European Integration
POLI 327.description: Post-1945 integration of Europe, comparison of national politics and attitudes to integration, and the history and institutions of the European Union.
POLI 327.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 328.title: Topics in Comparative Politics
POLI 328.description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the departmental website.
POLI 328.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 329.title: Gender and Politics
POLI 329.description: Relations between gender and political processes and institutions, including the impact of globalization and economic development.
POLI 329.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 330.title: Japanese Political Economy
POLI 330.description: Issues in contemporary Japanese political economy, including industrial policy, the Keiretsu groupings, the main-bank system, trends toward deregulation, and business-labour relations.
POLI 330.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 331.title: Korean Government and Politics
POLI 331.description: An introduction to the politics of Korea. The evolution of Korean politics from authoritarian rule to democratic transition, focusing on present and future political, economic and social issues.
POLI 331.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 332.title: Politics and Government of Latin America
POLI 332.description: A comparative examination of democracy and authoritarianism in Latin America: populism, corporatism, bureaucratic authoritarianism, transitions from authoritarianism, and contemporary debates on the quality and diversity of democratic institutions.
POLI 332.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 333.title: Issues in Comparative Politics
POLI 333.description: An examination of a major issue in comparative politics (e.g., the media, gender, nationalism, ethnic conflict). Topics will vary from year to year.
POLI 333.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 334.title: Comparative Democratization
POLI 334.description: Literatures and theories on regime democratization around the world; the roles of political, economic, social, and international factors in encouraging or impeding democratization.
POLI 334.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 335.title: Comparative Federalism
POLI 335.description: An empirical and normative analysis of federalism as a way of structuring political life in industrialized democracies, investigating explanations for the design, persistence and operation of federal systems.
POLI 335.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 336.title: Associations and the State in Comparative Perspective
POLI 336.description: How organised groups (civil society organizations, NGOs, interest groups) interact with governments in a variety of countries.
POLI 336.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 337.title: The U.S. Presidency in Comparative Perspective
POLI 337.description: Executive leadership of the U.S. presidency in comparison to the leadership of other Anglo-American systems, including the U.K., Canada, and Australia.
POLI 337.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 338.title: Politics and Development
POLI 338.description: The relationship between political institutions and economic growth. How governments shape economic policy and development aid.
POLI 338.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 340.title: History of Political Ideas
POLI 340.description: An introduction to the political ideas of leading political philosophers from Ancient Greece to the 19th century.
POLI 340.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or above

POLI 341.title: Contemporary Political Theory
POLI 341.description: Topics may include freedom, colonialism, capitalism, Critical Theory and ideology, power and knowledge, social justice, rationalism, gender and identity politics, and the political.
POLI 341.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 342.title: Modern Political Theory: Analysis of a Selected Theorist
POLI 342.description: A detailed examination of an acknowledged masterpiece of modern political theory. The text and attendant literature vary from year to year. Consult the departmental website.
POLI 342.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 343.title: Theories of State and Society
POLI 343.description: Classical origins of contemporary theories of the state, market, and civil society, focused on the relationship between social order, politics, and democracy. Readings from Smith, Tocqueville, Weber, and contemporary sources.
POLI 343.prerequisiteText: All of POLI_V 100, POLI_V 101, POLI_V 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 344.title: Social and Political Thought
POLI 344.description: An examination of some of the major concepts in political philosophy such as justice, equality, rights, obligation, liberty in the context of both classical and contemporary political thought.
POLI 344.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 345.title: Gender and Politics: Political Thought and Practice
POLI 345.description: The role of gender in Western political theory and the implications for the practice of politics.
POLI 345.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 346.title: Democratic Theory
POLI 346.description: An examination of both classical and contemporary theories of democracy. Representative democratic theory, participatory democratic theory, and their relationship to twentieth century concepts of democracy.
POLI 346.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 347.title: Law and Political Theory
POLI 347.description: An examination of law and political theory that considers topics such as sovereignty, constitutionalism, civil disobedience, rights and the political role of judges.
POLI 347.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 348.title: Political Theory and Public Policy
POLI 348.description: Application of frameworks to policy questions that factor in debates about citizenship and social inclusion, and an examination of contemporary normative frameworks that fall along, and transcend, the left-right political spectrum.
POLI 348.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 350.title: Public Policy
POLI 350.description: An introduction to public policy: rationales for government intervention, the influence of interest groups and political institutions on policy outcomes, and the various stages in the policy process.
POLI 350.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 351.title: Environmental Politics and Policy
POLI 351.description: Domestic and international determinants of environmental policy; alternative approaches to environmental protection. The sustainable development paradigm; public opinion and interest group pressures; risk assessment; mandatory, voluntary and market-based policy instruments.
POLI 351.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 352.title: Comparative Politics of Public Policy
POLI 352.description: Policy making across industrialized democracies, with a focus on North America and Europe.
POLI 352.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 353.title: Public Opinion and Public Policy
POLI 353.description: The interaction of public opinion and public policies of climate change, inequality, poverty, and democratic institutions and values in Canada and other democracies.
POLI 353.prerequisiteText: Two of POLI_V 100, POLI_V 101, POLI_V 110, POLI_V 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 360.title: Security Studies
POLI 360.description: The contemporary international security context: reorientation of the study of security, patterns of inter- and intrastate conflict and communal violence, dilemmas of international response and conflict management.
POLI 360.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 361.title: International Violence and Its Control
POLI 361.description: A study of the nature of international violence from guerrilla to nuclear war; a survey of theories of the causes of interstate war; recent research findings on the causes of war and conditions for peace; a comparative analysis of strategies for controlling violence through disarmament and the promotion of alternative means of conflict resolution.
POLI 361.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 362.title: The Great Powers and International Politics
POLI 362.description: An examination of the changing nature of Great Power relations, including procedures and institutions for managing their conflicts, in the pre-Cold War, Cold War, and post-Cold War international systems.
POLI 362.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 363.title: Canadian Foreign Policy
POLI 363.description: An analysis of Canadian foreign policy on important international issues since the 1960s and of the policy-making process. Issues may include defence commitments, economic relations, activities of international organizations, and relations with the US, Europe, USSR, Asia and the Third World.
POLI 363.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 364.title: International Organizations
POLI 364.description: Analysis of the activities and influence of modern international organizations in international security, economic, and social issue areas. The course will focus on organizations associated with the United Nations, but other world and regional bodies will be analysed as well.
POLI 364.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 365.title: Asian International Relations
POLI 365.description: Analysis of the foreign policies of one or more of the states of East, Southeast, and South Asia; their relations with other states in the region as well as with major outside powers.
POLI 365.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 366.title: International Political Economy
POLI 366.description: An analysis of governmental policies and international political bargaining in regard to such issues as international investment, trade, and monetary relations.
POLI 366.prerequisiteText: Two of POLI_V 100, POLI_V 101, POLI_V 110, POLI_V 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 367.title: International Relations Theory and the International System
POLI 367.description: The evolution of the international system and empirical and normative theories of international relations such as realism, liberalism, and Marxism.
POLI 367.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 368.title: Topics in International Relations
POLI 368.description: Topics will vary from year to year. Consult the program website ( for more information.
POLI 368.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 369.title: Topics in International Security
POLI 369.description: Possible topics include armed conflict, terrorism, environmental change, or international crime. Topics vary year to year, see www.politics.ubc.ca/courses. Pre-requisite: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or above.

POLI 370.title: Topics in International Conflict Management
POLI 370.description: Problems of managing conflict in the international system. Possible topics include intervention, mediation, or sanctions. Topics vary year to year; see www.politics.ubc.ca/courses. Pre-requisite: Two of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or above.

POLI 371.title: Humanitarian Engineering: Politics and Practice
POLI 371.description: An interdisciplinary study of best practice, politics, and ethics associated with technical solutions to humanitarian assistance within Canada and abroad; examines policies used in aid and development contexts with emphasis on the application of engineering. Restricted to students with a Major, Combined Major, Honours, Honours with, or Minor specialization in Political Science or International Relations, or at least third-year standing in any BASc program.

POLI 372.title: Multinational Corporations and Globalization
POLI 372.description: Multinational corporations and the state in the contemporary international system, including the impact of multinationals and foreign direct investment on governments, societies, and industry.
POLI 372.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 373.title: Ethics in World Politics
POLI 373.description: When is it right to wage war? Who should pay for global warming? Should the wealthy provide foreign aid- how much? Analysis of traditions of moral thought to reach reasoned judgments about such dilemmas in global politics.
POLI 373.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 374.title: International Peacekeeping
POLI 374.description: The development of peacekeeping within and outside the United Nations system and as an instrument of conflict management.
POLI 374.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 375.title: Global Environmental Politics
POLI 375.description: Ecological consequences of the global political economy.
POLI 375.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 376.title: International Law
POLI 376.description: The nature, sources, and sanctions of international law; the notion of nationhood with particular reference to the status of the British Dominions; territorial and extra-territorial jurisdiction; diplomatic and sovereign immunities; international delinquency; treaties; settlement of disputes; international organizations. This course may not be taken for credit in both Arts and Law.
POLI 376.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 377.title: Nuclear Weapons and Arms Control
POLI 377.description: Evolution and contemporary significance of nuclear weapons and arms control policy and technology from the perspective of the physical and life sciences and the social sciences and humanities.
POLI 377.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 378.title: The Politics of Terrorism
POLI 378.description: Exploration of contemporary terrorism as a contested area of understanding and as a social construct. Includes origins and motives, evolution of terrorist groups, strategies and tactics, and anti-terrorism and counter-terrorism responses.
POLI 378.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 379.title: China in World Politics
POLI 379.description: Impact and implications of the rise of China in historical and contemporary perspective.
POLI 379.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 110, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 380.title: Quantitative Methods in Political Science
POLI 380.description: An introduction to quantitative research methods and data analysis used in the study of politics. Students are advised to review the Science Credit Exclusion Lists for course equivalencies to avoid unnecessary registration.
POLI 380.prerequisiteText: POLI_V 110. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 381.title: Managing Quantitative Data in Political Science
POLI 381.description: The basics of quantitative analysis and managing data in Political Science, including the sourcing, construction, cleaning, manipulation, and visualization of data sets.

POLI 385.title: Public Opinion and Elections
POLI 385.description: Psychological and social foundations of public opinion; quality of democratic decision-making; how voters make up their minds; impact of electoral systems; social bases of party systems; campaigns and the mass media. The Canadian experience in comparative context.
POLI 385.prerequisiteText: All of POLI 100, POLI 101, POLI 240. Or third-year standing or higher

POLI 390.title: Honours Seminar
POLI 390.description: An examination of the dimensions of Political Science and the major debates within the discipline. Restricted to students with an Honours or Honours with specialization in Political Science.

POLI 395.title: Political Science in Practice
POLI 395.description: The practical application of political science capacities and knowledge. Restricted to Political Science and International Relations Majors and Minors. Pass/Fail

POLI 401.title: Canadian Provincial and Regional Politics
POLI 401.description: Seminar examines political parties, processes, and institutions in the provincial political systems and regional arrangements between provinces. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 402.title: Law and Politics of the Canadian Constitution
POLI 402.description: Seminar on the origins and development of the Canadian Constitution: the political aspects of federalism and the legal consequences of the Charter of Rights. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 403.title: The Political Economy of Canada
POLI 403.description: A seminar devoted to the analysis of the interplay of economic and social factors in the shaping of Canadian politics: the major issues and strains in the functioning of the Canadian polity. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 404.title: Public Policy and Its Administration
POLI 404.description: Political and administrative aspects of public policy, particularly in Canada. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 405.title: Advanced Topics in Canadian Politics
POLI 405.description: Important topics in Canadian politics and public policies. Possible topics include elections, gender and identity, or media. Topics vary year to year; see www.politics.ubc.ca/courses. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or above.

POLI 406.title: Indigenous Peoples and Canadian Politics
POLI 406.description: Seminar in political structures, activities, and demands of Indigenous peoples; policies of federal, provincial, and territorial governments; relations between these governments and Indigenous peoples; role of the courts and the Constitution. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 420.title: Advanced Topics in Comparative Politics
POLI 420.description: An important topic involving politics, policies, and political systems around the world including, for example, ethnic politics, development, and the growth and erosion of democracy. Topics vary year to year; see www.politics.ubc.ca/courses. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 422.title: Selected Problems in Comparative Politics
POLI 422.description: A seminar devoted to intensive analysis of a contemporary political problem from a comparative perspective, e.g., ethnic politics, class politics, the politics of post-industrial society. For specific content in a given year, consult the departmental website. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 423.title: Issues in Comparative Politics
POLI 423.description: Seminar in comparative analysis of constitutionalism, authoritarianism, democracy, etc. For specific content in a given year, consult the departmental website. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 424.title: Ethics in Democratic Politics
POLI 424.description: Ethics in politics, including citizenship and public service, and practices demanded by the institutions of democracy. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 426.title: Seminar on Comparative Parties and Party Systems
POLI 426.description: Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 427.title: Advanced Topics in Chinese Politics and Development
POLI 427.description: Topics in Chinese politics and public policies. Possible topics include environmental politics, local government, or state-society relations from a comparative perspective. Topics vary year to year; see www.politics.ubc.ca/courses. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or above.

POLI 428.title: Comparative Public Management
POLI 428.description: Major changes in the structures and processes of government in advanced democracies, including the welfare state, citizenship, ethics, accountability, and institutional reform. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 429.title: Seminar in Issues in Gender and Politics
POLI 429.description: Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 439.title: Politics and Economic Growth
POLI 439.description: The relationship between politics, economics, and development. The role of the state, political institutions, economic policy, and foreign aid in development strategies. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 440.title: Contemporary Political Theory
POLI 440.description: Examines the political ideas of leading contemporary political philosophers. Topics vary year to year; see www.politics.ubc.ca/courses. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 441.title: Interpretation and Criticism in Political Theory
POLI 441.description: Approaches to political criticism: Critical Theory, Foucauldian genealogy, critical realism, and feminism, including forms of domination, which shape people's beliefs and self-conceptions. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 442.title: Contemporary Political Theorists: Analysis of a Selected Theorist
POLI 442.description: This seminar examines in detail the political ideas of an important political philosopher of the twentieth century. The theorist studied varies from year to year. Consult the departmental website. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 443.title: Modern Western Political Thought
POLI 443.description: Seminar: Texts in the history of modern Western political thought, such as works by Thomas Hobbes, John Locke, Jean-Jacques Rousseau, Karl Marx, Alexis de Tocqueville, John Stuart Mill, Friedrich Nietzsche, Max Weber, and Sigmund Freud. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 445.title: Critical Theory: Political Theory and the Problems of Race
POLI 445.description: Traditions of critical social theory, broadly construed, to examine the modern politics of 'race,' racism, and racialized identities. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 446.title: Multiculturalism and Identity Politics
POLI 446.description: Seminar will examine how identity is theorized in contemporary political thought, beginning with the role that identity plays in the western canon and proceeding to examine feminist, multicultural, queer, and post-colonial theories of citizenship along with their critics. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 448.title: Democratic Theory
POLI 448.description: Overview of traditional democratic theory with close readings of several contemporary theories, such as those of Habermas, Rawls, and Arendt. Readings are drawn from complete original texts, and assessment is based on a research essay. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 449.title: Topics in Political Theory
POLI 449.description: Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 450.title: Policy Analysis
POLI 450.description: Analytical tools and practical policy analysis to address real-world issues for clients or employers. Involves collecting and analyzing policy-relevant data, generating alternatives, and evaluating trade-offs. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 460.title: Foreign Policy Analysis
POLI 460.description: A seminar devoted to the analysis of the foreign policies of one or more states, as well as to the study of literature pertaining to foreign policy analysis. For specific content in a given year, consult the departmental website. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 461.title: Peace and Conflict Studies
POLI 461.description: A seminar on a selected topic concerning the causes of war and strategies for the promotion of peace. For specific content in a given year, consult the departmental website. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 462.title: International Relations Theory
POLI 462.description: This seminar examines some of the major theoretical approaches to the study of international relations. For specific content in a given year, consult the departmental website. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 463.title: International Interdependence
POLI 463.description: Topics and public policies relating to international economic relations. Topics vary year to year; see www.politics.ubc.ca/courses. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or above.

POLI 464.title: Advanced Topics in International Relations
POLI 464.description: Topics and public policies related to interactions between states and non-state actors, such as armed conflict management or international institutions. Topics vary year to year; see www.politics.ubc.ca/courses. One section (3 credits) reserved for fourth-year International Relations Majors. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or above.

POLI 466.title: The Politics of International Law
POLI 466.description: Seminar on the origins and politics of international law, and its impact on international affairs; the laws of war, human rights, environment, law of the sea, and international criminal law. Restricted to students in fourth-year standing or higher.

POLI 482.title: Data and Models Capstone
POLI 482.description: Seminar on data analysis and modeling in Political Science. Restricted to Certificate in Data and Models in Political Science students.

POLI 492.title: Honours Thesis
POLI 492.description: In consultation with faculty, students develop a research project, report on their project during seminars, give feedback on their fellow students' projects, and write a thesis. Restricted to students with an Honours or Honours with specialization in Political Science. Fourth-year standing or higher required.

POLI 500.title: Professional Development in Political Science
POLI 500.description: Pass/Fail. Evidence-based practices and tools for academic and non-academic paths in the political science profession as well as identifying alternative career possibilities. Includes potential alignment with personal strengths and self-awareness. Restricted to students in the following programs: PhD in Political Science, MA in Political Science.
